## Design

### 2026-10-11 – I'm new to PCB deigns so I followed the guide posted on https://github.com/SharKingStudios/Starbie/blob/main/Week%201%20Guide.md to start my Starbie project.

**9h**

I'm new to PCB deigns so I followed the guide posted on https://github.com/SharKingStudios/Starbie/blob/main/Week%201%20Guide.md to start my Starbie project.
The guide was pretty clear except for some things I'll be mentioning here.

First wall I hit was that I didn't install the libraries before starting my schematics which AI helped with that.

The next thing was my schematics, I didn't add the no-connect flag to the unconnected pins and the power flag to the ground and voltage pins, so I added them and it was done:

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 1134481](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/d00cfefdd715d32f168dff230f777777f027d3a6c07e3eba6887ce711167bb7c.png)
But it was just a  minor thing really, AI helped with that and I fixed it, I also grouped and arranged my designs:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/6f7233f0ab1bc7bc68c6c9445cb2d58fb7bba32f4b03ab61c26f1f5d983afaa0.png)
I then made sure my schematic footprints were added:

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 010807](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/dacd71f6fd32aec07b45f0b0b2fcfa02994e3305d8098560473961cf0f24bb05.png)
By manually selecting each of those lines and searching for the right footprint it was easy:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/e84e2f5b414f3af48c034ab9201111c25af7545dae6657050f33151da22eeb4b.png)

Next up was to create the PCB from the schematics which was easy, just use the drefault settings:
![Screenshot 2026-10-10 011819](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/0f290050a2960b2efcc7e9766d3872f032c6d5be0c350537062eb480638dff82.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 012229](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/1ddc119c5ecb5a1caa0aa2ab64b1de9fe385daa703cd6a20c4d1afc540307fc4.png)

For creating the outline I used paint to draw the star, saved it as a png file and used image converter in KiCad to create the outline for my PCB then copied it from the image converter and pasted it to the PCB layout. Everything else went fine but it took me a lot of time since I'm new to it. I eventually ended up with this:

![Screenshot 2026-10-10 104908](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/ed96660001ef2b0d07159c1392a677c9432a5858725dfd3f656b3cfa13647bed.png)
_(Adding the ground pour was a little tricky, after following the recommended Youtube giude provided in the Starbie guide, press B on your keyboard to refill the zones)_
![Screenshot 2026-10-11 112951](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/eb4f21715d6c52b4d99da85fc8bfec1bf1651af04cf0ae5d5f10598972275ddd.png)

Once the PCB was done I had to check for errors and I got this error: Track [+3.3V] on B.Cu has unconnected end. It turned out that for some reasons, the +3.3V track on my ESP32 board (pin 12) didn't connect to the cpper trace beneath it. I was routing it from other pins too and they worked so I don't know why it didn't work for this pin so I just fixed it by extending a trace from it and using a via to connect it to the copper trace beneath it the deleting the excess trace:
![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/8572bcee29956b439d4079ee2c2399d501d5996365024736f473c158966c6943.png)
Once this was done, I just created the gaber and drill files and checked them:
![Screenshot 2026-10-11 123111](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/2PBCqhowNk9URkIH6vXUAeh46r9i4Wol/7b636c915c9c2c98ba50dd80411dd76ac2a57e7f3e892f4804e5f8b94cd546a5.png)

I also generated the BOM file and with that, I was done with my firest ever PCB design.
